faqs.question: Why take HLA typing DQ locus Class II Test?
faqs.answer: This test is done to rule diseases strongly linked to DQ locus. For e.g., coeliac disease, narcolepsy

faqs.question: Is this test for you?
faqs.answer: Performed for patients suspected of having diseases strongly associated with the HLA-DQ locus for e.g. coeliac disease

faqs.question: More Info on HLA typing DQ locus Class II Test
faqs.answer: Celiac disease (CD) is a multifactorial immune-mediated disease.Specific HLA-DQ genes have been recognized as necessary factors for the occurrence of Celiac Disease (CD). This test provides genotyping for detection of HLA-DQ2 (DQA1*05:01 or 05:05 and DQB1*02:01 or 02:02) and HLA-DQ8 (DQB1*03:02). The HLA-DQB1*02:01 allele is present in more than 90% CD children. In the perspective of a widened pediatric population screening for CD, a double-step process might be suggested: HLA-DQB1*02:01 might be investigated first and, only if this result is positive, children might be candidate for a prospective serologic screening, as a second step
